tracking: Coordinator owns Beads. This source-bound design receipt proposes a subsequent dispatch, not an independent issue tracker or new owner permission request.

current_boundary.internal_activation: New .29.2.2 internal activation uses fresh production exclusion, native-proof orchestration, both exact authenticated staged-factor readbacks and explicit transaction observation. Host and runtime evidence are still being assembled by coordinator; this plan does not claim their terminal result.
current_boundary.legacy_unmodified: rewrapWith still wraps the destructive legacy path in ordinary RecoveryKeyAdmission. The v2 refusal guard remains. No production public recovery caller is wired to the new internal activation.
current_boundary.current_UI: VaultFactorRecoveryScreen calls unlockSurvivingFactor only. It deliberately does not rewrap or reset. Preserve this bounded access-only route; do not turn its existing unchanged-vault messages into claims about an activation attempt.

concrete_remaining_risks.risk: Surviving-factor unwrap is followed by deleteEntry(dead fixed alias) and createKey before new-factor auth or storage.rewrap. Cancellation/failure can leave old envelope bytes referring to replaced old key material.

Per-provider mutex/ordinary admission allows multiple providers simultaneously; a final generation check does not undo earlier alias writes. Late auth after lock can mutate aliases/files before the outer guard cancels delivery.

Per-storage-instance mutex, fixed-alias v1 rewrite and best-effort parent sync do not retain full generations or explicit possible-rename outcomes. Do not route existing-envelope recovery through this primitive.
KDoc promises dead alias deletion only after commit and a live currentKey on success. The former is false for current code; the latter is incompatible with locked metadata-only activation.

Success requires nonnull currentKey, mints AuthorizationToken, sets Unlocked and notifies listeners; its catch branches currently conflate cancellation/error with a retryable recovery failure. A committed or unknown activation cannot use these branches unchanged.

recommended_order: Finish and freeze .29.2.2 source, negative controls and separately scoped encrypted synthetic-runtime evidence first. Keep real Android per-use authentication/app/physical gates open.
Coordinator selects the explicit locked result contract below before dispatching .29.2.4. Preserve the surviving-factor access-only UI unchanged.

Implement one internal closed recovery operation that obtains the surviving candidate, prepares fresh unique aliases, and activates through the existing proof/auth transaction under one production reservation; never call the old fixed-alias rewrap.
Migrate public provider/session outcomes and exhaustive fakes/tests together, so no transient integration maps metadata activation to legacy Success.
Only after core migration passes, dispatch .29.2.3 explicit app recovery entry/prompt lifecycle/uncertain outcome handling. Physical .29.3 remains separate.

proposed_result_contract.decision_owner: Coordinator; no renewed owner permission is needed for this internal implementation design.
proposed_result_contract.preferred: RewrapResult.ActivatedNeedsNormalUnlock(newKeyVersion, durability) plus RewrapResult.ActivationNeedsInspection(transactionId). Neither result contains key bytes, AuthorizationToken or an unlocked flag.
proposed_result_contract.legacy_success: Do not reinterpret old RewrapResult.Success as metadata activation. Remove/replace it in the coordinated migration, or retain it solely for explicitly isolated legacy implementations with no production caller; do not leave a destructive production fallback.

mapping.manager: Remain/transition Locked, clear all currentKey and authorization token/session authority, clear stale failed-factor routing only after known activation. No onUnlocked notification.
Remain locked and disclose visible-new/durability-uncertain status. Never auto-rollback, delete old aliases or claim unchanged.

mapping.internal: Observed(UNKNOWN), or result delivery lost after entering activation
mapping.manager: No token/key/session; persist only a non-secret attempt identifier or discover retained attempt metadata on restart. Fresh exclusive observation is required before displaying old/new state.

mapping.public: Explicit NotActivated/unchanged-active observation, preserving retained partial attempt
mapping.manager: Remain locked; no automatic reuse of the consumed transaction UUID.

mapping.internal: Pretransaction ProofRejected, auth cancellation or Unavailable with proven no entry into transaction
mapping.manager: Remain locked. Do not overgeneralize this message to cancellation after possible rename.

proposed_result_contract.cancellation_delivery: Even an internally correct Observed result may be discarded by a cancelled parent/Deferred. Catching CancellationException around the public call does not prove no mutation. Retained exact old/new evidence and fresh-lease reconcile support observation, never a new capability. Do not use NonCancellable to publish keys/tokens or continue authentication after lock.
proposed_result_contract.normal_unlock: After a known activation, ordinary provider v2 unlock must independently authenticate its exact selected Cipher and receive ordinary admission. Only that ordinary unlock can mint a token or open the vault.

closed_operation_design.continuous_admission: Prefer one production recovery Reservation across candidate extraction, preparation and activation. Refactor only internal leased helpers; existing prepareWith/activateWith wrappers keep their consume/zero and independent fresh-proof/fresh-auth semantics. No nested ordinary admission and no acquireRecovery while an ordinary reservation is held.
closed_operation_design.why_naive_chaining_fails: Calling today's prepareWith and activateWith sequentially releases the lease between them. A lock in that gap invalidates no reservation, so a later newly acquired reservation could continue an operation the owner just cancelled. Releasing candidate-read ordinary admission and then acquiring exclusive also needs an explicit operation-generation/cancellation handoff. A simple alias-order edit or late ensureActive is insufficient.
closed_operation_design.candidate_extraction: Under the live closed recovery reservation, freeze/read the actual v1 active bytes, create the surviving fixed-alias decrypt Cipher, authenticate that exact instance, revalidate lease/active bytes, unwrap exactly32 bytes, and keep candidate private. Missing/invalidated/locked material remains typed refusal. Never populate provider.master or expose candidate to caller/session.
closed_operation_design.preparation: Use fresh UUID aliases for BOTH factors with unchanged StrongBox policy. Keep original fixed aliases/envelope/ciphertext intact. Four fresh preparation crypto operations remain authenticated/readback checked; a Prepared receipt remains evidence only.
closed_operation_design.activation: Invoke internal activation in the same live operation with its own fresh ciphertext snapshot/native proof and two fresh exact-Cipher factor decrypt/readbacks. Same-candidate availability is not a substitute for that repeated proof/auth. Keep whole-file hashing and fsync outside revocation monitor.
closed_operation_design.retention: No deleteEntry on old fixed aliases or on staged/new aliases in failure cleanup. No old/new envelope deletion, rollback, owner reset or ciphertext rewrite. A failed UUID stays consumed; another attempt needs a new UUID and all fresh proofs/auth.
closed_operation_design.lease_ownership: A coordinator owns closing its Reservation once. Leased helpers must not close caller-owned reservations; wrappers own their internally acquired lease. Prefer accepting the actual production Reservation type internally where feasible, avoiding a public arbitrary-lease authority route.
closed_operation_design.alias_limit: Check detectable expected-alias absence before activation. No facade/API currently attests immutable hardware alias generation; external invalidation after a successful readback remains a later ordinary-unlock concern.
closed_operation_design.initial_scope: v1-to-v2 only; do not silently generalize this flow into arbitrary v2-to-v2 rotation, setup/reset, or export migration.

worker_core_slice.change: NEW internal continuous-lease orchestrator for surviving-factor candidate acquisition and staged recovery, with no session publication.
Bounded internal leased preparation helper while preserving public-internal stage-only wrapper semantics and existing tests.
Bounded internal leased activation helper while preserving fresh proof/both-factor auth and explicit outcome/cancellation behavior.
Remove destructive production rewrap path and route closed recovery to the orchestrator; no fallback to fixed-alias storage.rewrap.
Wire concrete recovery dependency from canonical VaultPaths into production provider; no default/security-policy changes.

tests: exact exhaustive app/feature fake callers found by compile if public result variants change
excluded_until_app_child: No current UI route change, new owner flow, physical work, hosted dispatch or default/model/runtime switch in .29.2.4 core implementation.
proposed_file_ownership.conditional: If coordinator chooses explicit operation-generation handoff instead of continuous reservation, RecoveryKeyAdmission/VaultRecoveryExclusion changes need separate reviewed ownership and deterministic gap-lock races; do not add them opportunistically.

required_verification: For each surviving factor, no fixed alias create/delete occurs on success, cancel, storage/auth failure or late callback; old envelopes and ciphertext plus both old aliases stay byte/material equivalent.
Two provider instances and reset/open concurrently: one continuous owner, all other admissions refused; lock between extraction/preparation/activation revokes the operation before any later mutation.

Wrong candidate for this vault fails native proof even after valid surviving-factor authentication. Exact-Cipher substitution, bad key length, opposite AAD, missing aliases and stage/source tampering fail closed.
Existing preparation and activation suites retain all identities and fail-closed boundaries after leased-helper refactor. No bulk hashing/fsync migrates under the revocation monitor.
Success/uncertain/unknown public outcomes always leave currentKey null, authorizationToken null and no unlocked observer. Later normal unlock obtains fresh authentication and admission.
Actual Job.cancel after rename plus a discarded Deferred result never produces an unchanged-vault claim; fresh coordinator/lease reconcile identifies current bytes without token or auth authority.
Failure before/after rename and directory sync retains both generations, reports uncertainty accurately and never retries a consumed UUID or automatically deletes/reset/rolls back.

Meaningful negative controls: restoring fixed-alias predelete; mapping Activated to old Success; releasing/reacquiring lease without operation generation; mapping postrename cancellation to UserCancelled. Original assertions must fail and restored source must match before final checks.

Coordinator serialized offline lint, both full core vault host variants, affected session/app/feature contract tests and both instrumentation compiles; inspect actual XML/source/hash receipts. Actual per-use Android authentication and process-crash acceptance require separately bounded synthetic runtime fixtures.

acceptance_split.29.2.4_core: Implementation/host review may accept absence of destructive legacy mutation and locked public results. It does not accept a usable owner recovery UI or real per-use hardware authentication.
acceptance_split.29.2.3_app_runtime: Explicit mutation intent, both-factor prompting/cancellation, activity recreation, unknown commit wording/reinspection and independent normal unlock, with synthetic vault fixtures only.
acceptance_split.29.3_physical: Sole designated runner, current connection and normal owner unlock; separate exact artifact/install/readback and physical acceptance. No owner vault reset/content action.
acceptance_split.power_loss: Injected host exceptions and process termination/restart do not prove power-loss durability.
